propositions: Three near-duplicate detached-child spawn implementations exist across push.py, enrich_drain.py, and compact_trigger.py, each independently reimplementing PYTHONPATH bootstrap, detach flags, stdio discipline, and cwd handling.
A single omission (missing cwd= parameter) propagated across all three sites via deliberate code imitation, demonstrating that duplicated spawn logic causes defects to multiply.

A consolidated spawn_detached helper in _proc.py should own bootstrap/detach/cwd logic while remaining stdlib-only and re-raising on failure, allowing per-caller exception handling and env construction to remain independent.

The four acceptance criteria require exactly one detached-spawn implementation testable via static source scan, a recorded decision on repo_root's cwd fallback posture, and preservation of _proc.py as a stdlib-only leaf.
A fourth copy-paste site (gc_trigger.py) landed concurrently, confirming the structural need for centralized spawn logic and completing the consolidation scope to include multi-arg generalization.
